overview: Cao Wei was the most powerful of the Three Kingdoms, controlling the northern heartland of China. Founded by Cao Cao's son Cao Pi, it inherited the Han administrative system and produced significant literary and military achievements.

items.text: The Cao family created some of the finest poetry of the period, establishing the Jian'an literary style.
Cao Pi writes the first systematic treatise on Chinese literary criticism.
Ma Jun invents the south-pointing chariot, a mechanical compass vehicle using differential gears.
Tuntian system of military-agricultural colonies settled frontier regions.
Administrative innovations passed to the Jin dynasty.
The Romance of the Three Kingdoms novel later romanticized this era.

fall.text: Sima Yan forced the last Wei emperor to abdicate and founded the Jin dynasty.
